standard_text: Utilization of electricity: current, voltage and resistance in household circuits; series and parallel wiring; electrical power and energy in kilowatt-hours; reading electricity bills and using electricity safely and efficiently. body_html:
How to think about it

Electric current flows when a voltage pushes charges through a closed circuit. Ohm's law: V = IR. Homes are wired in parallel so that every appliance gets 230 V and can be switched on and off separately. Fuses and circuit breakers cut the current when it is too large.

Electrical power P = VI tells how fast an appliance uses energy. Energy used = power × time; the electricity company charges per kilowatt-hour (kWh). Using efficient appliances such as LED bulbs and inverter air conditioners, and unplugging devices, saves energy and money.

Example

A 1,500 W flat iron is used for 2 h. Energy used?

1.5 kW × 2 h

Answer: 3 kWh

Example

A 230 V appliance draws 5 A. Power?

P = VI

Answer: 1,150 W

Common mistakes

  • Thinking current is used up in a circuit.
  • Mixing up kW and kWh.
  • Overloading an extension cord with many appliances.

faq.a: Each appliance gets the full voltage and works on its own.

faq.q: Why is it dangerous to touch switches with wet hands?
faq.a: Water lowers the skin's resistance, so a dangerous current can flow.
